properties.description:
`crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_server_keeps_the_export_current.rs`, four tests on a real RocksDB store — real because the hand-edit baseline is recorded against the graph path, and a memory-backed service would exercise a different path than the one that ships.

1. A write reaches disk with nobody calling export_graph. The feature; without it the guarantee is a claim.
2. Ten writes spread 300 ms apart still cost one export. The debounce is what makes this affordable.
3. A hand edit survives untouched, AND loop_status carries the reason — both the `auto_export.skipped` field and an entry in `next`, because a guarantee that has silently stopped guaranteeing is worse than none.
4. A read-only server refuses the write-through and reports no status.

⚠️ TEST 2 WAS CAUGHT LYING AND REWRITTEN, and the note is on the test itself. The obvious version — ten writes back to back — passed with the debounce set to ZERO, because the task has not been scheduled yet and the pokes collapse: it was measuring the scheduler, not the feature. Spacing the writes is what makes it discriminate.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: the behaviour of two servers pointed at one file, and anything about the git anchor (that is ver:the-export-chains-from-main).
properties.findings: All four pass. Both guards were shown to FAIL before being trusted: disabling the hand-edit check makes test 3 fail on the assertion that the edit survived; setting the quiet period to zero makes test 2 report 10 exports against a ceiling of 2. The full mcp suite — 64 test binaries — passes alongside, with toolsnap, smoke_mcp, empty_speaks and refusal_speaks green and 180 tool schemas unchanged.
properties.name: A write reaches the file unasked, a burst costs one export, and a hand edit survives
